title: Which statement is which?

prereqs.why: The whole question is reading which event is being conditioned on.
Bayes is what relates the two conditionals, and why they differ.

statement:
In a large population, $\P(\text{owns a car} \mid \text{has a driving licence}) = 0.8$.

Which **one** of the following must also be true?
hints: Read each option as a sentence about who is in the restricted population. $\P(A \mid B)$ is about the $B$ people only.
Three of the options claim something about $\P(\text{licence} \mid \text{car})$ or about unconditional probabilities. Could those be computed from the one number you were given?
You were told one conditional. Its complement *within the same condition* is forced; anything that changes which side of the bar an event is on is not.

options: $\P(\text{does not own a car} \mid \text{has a licence}) = 0.2$
$80\%$ of the population owns a car.
$\P(\text{owns a car and has a licence}) = 0.8$
